### Questioning God's Lot
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/questioning-gods-lot
Passage: Joshua 17:14
Points:
- The tribes of Joseph complained that their single territorial share was inadequate for their numbers.
- They likely sought special treatment from Joshua, but he reminded them that God assigned each allotment.
- When confronted with enemy chariots and forested land, they looked for an easy expansion instead of fighting.
- Joshua told them that their portion was sufficient if they were willing to labor and clear the land.
- Believers must trust God's sovereign placement and faithfully obey Him through trials and ease alike.

### When Your Life Is Too Full for God
Author: Adrian Rogers
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/loveworthfinding/love-worth-finding-january-2-2026.html
Passage: Joshua 17:15
Points:
- Joshua directed the sons of Joseph to clear the forest if their territory felt too confined.
- Many Christians fail to experience spiritual victory because their schedules are overcrowded.
- Being too busy for prayer and Scripture reading reveals involvement in things God never assigned.
- Even benign or good activities become harmful when they crowd out devotion to the Lord.
- Believers must deliberately eliminate clutter to protect daily time spent at Jesus' feet.

### Faith in Difficult Times
Author: L. B. Cowman
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/desert/streams-in-the-desert-february-13th.html
Passage: Joshua 17:18
Points:
- When valleys are blocked by difficult obstacles, believers are invited to ascend into higher spiritual ground.
- Even when earthly avenues of service close, prayer can move heaven and reach into eternity.
- God does not show us daunting tasks to mock us, but to spur us on to spiritual exploits.
- True faith possesses the capacity to clear dense forests through the strength of God's indwelling.
- Hardships are given to demonstrate what God accomplishes through praying, working faith.

### Bible Pathway - Mar. 19, 2010
Author: Bible Pathway Ministries
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathway-mar-19-2010-11627555.html
Passage: Joshua 17:14
Points:
- Ephraim and Manasseh complained that their territory was too small, expecting favoritism due to their size.
- Instead of conquering their full allotment by faith, they chose compromise and tolerated Canaanite presence.
- In contrast to their selfish grasping, Joshua waited until every tribe received land before taking a small inheritance.
- God calls believers to put away pride and greed, finding contentment in serving Him humbly.
